note: Synthetic cases built from real pricing and scope decisions. Firms and people are invented. Each assumes a profile with an 850 GBP day rate, a 700 GBP floor, 3 client days a week, and builds paid half on signing and half on acceptance.

evals.prompt: A friend who runs an events business asked me to 'knock up a small booking site'. We started last week without talking money. He's now asking for a gallery and a promo video page too. Write up where we are.
evals.expected_output: Raises budget and price now, before more work, and treats the gallery and video page as priced extras rather than absorbing them.
expectations: Says price and budget should be agreed now, not at the end
Treats the gallery and video page as optional priced extras
Does not send anything to the friend without the user's approval

evals.prompt: Mid-build on a signed workflow project (two connected systems: their CRM and inbox), the client asks us to also write results into their accounting system. They say it's 'just one more connection'.
evals.expected_output: Classifies it as a change because it adds a connected system, drafts a change note with price and effect on timeline and acceptance, and says work waits for written approval.
expectations: Classifies the request as out of scope
Drafts a change note with price and timeline effect
States that work starts only after written approval
Does not quietly absorb the work

evals.prompt: The client signed our 4,000 GBP proposal within ten minutes of receiving it, no questions. Great, right?
evals.expected_output: Celebrates the win, records it, and notes that an instant unnegotiated yes suggests the price was too low, so the next quote should go up.
expectations: Records the proposal as accepted
Says an instant yes suggests the price was low
Recommends raising the next comparable quote

evals.prompt: Write a proposal for a 15-day build starting next month. We have 4 free client days next month and 10 the month after.
evals.expected_output: Flags that 15 days doesn't fit next month and offers a later start or a first phase that fits.
expectations: Compares the 15 days against free capacity
Says it does not fit next month
Offers a later start or a smaller first phase

evals.prompt: Quote 3,000 GBP fixed for this. I estimate about 5 days of work.
evals.expected_output: Works out the effective day rate of 600 GBP, says it is below the 700 GBP floor, and suggests changing scope or price.
expectations: Calculates an effective day rate of 600 GBP
Says it is below the 700 GBP floor
Suggests changing scope or price, not the estimate

evals.prompt: Two weeks after go-live the client says the workflow stopped working because they renamed fields in their CRM. They want it fixed free under the defect period.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a failure caused by a change in the client's own systems is a change, not a defect, and drafts a change note.
expectations: Classifies it as a change caused by the client's systems
Does not treat it as a free defect fix
Drafts a change note for the user to approve

evals.prompt: Kestrel Homes already pays a lead-generation agency about 5,000 GBP a month. Their sales director asked on the call why they'd pay us as well. How should the proposal handle that?
evals.expected_output: Treats the existing spend as proof of the need, not an objection, and positions the work as complementing the agency: the gaps around it such as follow-up, people's time and repeated manual steps. Does not pitch replacing the agency.
expectations: Says the existing spend shows the need is real
Does not frame the agency as a competitor to replace
Proposes work that fills gaps around the existing provision
Invents none of Kestrel's figures beyond what was given

evals.prompt: A friend runs a small events business and wants us to start building their booking site this week. They said we can sort the price out later. Shall I just start?
evals.expected_output: Says to scope it and send a proposal with a price before any work starts, even for a friend, and offers to draft it. A friends and family discount, if any, is named against the full price.
expectations: Advises against starting before a proposal is agreed
Offers to scope and draft the proposal
If a discount is used, names it and shows the full price
Starts no work and sends nothing

evals.prompt: The buyer asked how our 6,000 GBP build compares with just paying for an off-the-shelf booking subscription. They sell about 400 tickets a year at 12 GBP. Put the comparison together.
evals.expected_output: Builds a cost model rather than an opinion: the build once, each route's running cost per year for five years with a cumulative total, and per-ticket fees at 12 GBP. Notes which jobs the subscription doesn't cover, prices it at the tier 400 tickets needs, keeps card fees in the row that pays them and gives payback against the subscription. Marks any figure it doesn't have as an assumption to confirm.
expectations: Compares year by year with a cumulative total, not one headline figure
Models the per-ticket fees at the buyer's 12 GBP price
Names any jobs the subscription route does not cover
Gives payback or the year the build becomes cheaper against the subscription
Marks unknown costs as assumptions instead of inventing them

evals.prompt: Proposal is 4,500 GBP for the build plus two optional extras at 600 GBP and 400 GBP. Draft the outline of the covering email.
evals.expected_output: Leads with the full offer including both extras, then shows the trim as a ladder (all in, one off, both off), states that the extras sit outside the 4,500 GBP total, and keeps to an outline with numbered parts rather than writing the email.
expectations: Leads with the full offer, not the stripped price
Shows the options as a ladder the buyer can pick from
Says the extras sit outside the headline total
Gives an outline, not finished email prose
Sends nothing

evals.prompt: We agreed 5,000 GBP total with the client. They now want the website line to go from 1,200 GBP to 1,500 GBP because we added a page. Update the proposal.
evals.expected_output: Holds the agreed 5,000 GBP total by moving another line down by 300 GBP, or flags that the total would otherwise change, tells the user which line moved, and lists every place the change must reach: cover price, subtotal, total, timeline and exclusions.
expectations: Keeps the agreed total, or asks the user before changing it
Says which line moved and by how much
Lists the other places in the document the change reaches
Does not send the updated proposal without approval
